title: Extensions of quasi-coherent modules on an algebraic space
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$, with its small etale site and structure sheaf $\mathcal O_X$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Module sheaves are [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and quasi-coherence is [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Let $0\to M\to N\to Q\to0$ be a short exact sequence in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. If $M$ and $Q$ are quasi-coherent, then $N$ is quasi-coherent. No quasi-compactness, separation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary object $u:T\to X$ of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$. Identify $X_{\mathrm{et}}/T$ with $T_{\mathrm{et}}$: an etale $T$-scheme maps to $X$ by composition, and a map between two etale $X$-schemes is etale by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. These inverse descriptions have the same scheme morphisms, jointly surjective coverings, and structure rings $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$. Restriction is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], so the given sequence restricts to $0\to M_T\to N_T\to Q_T\to0$. Both end terms are quasi-coherent: the local free presentations defining quasi-coherence restrict to every further slice, with the same covering families and free modules. We will prove $N_T$ quasi-coherent for this arbitrary $T$.

source.place: Tag 03M1, lemma-properties-quasi-coherent, introductory localization argument and proof of (4).

proof.text: Write $L=\epsilon_T^*$ and $R=\epsilon_{T,*}$, where $R$ is restriction to Zariski opens. By [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], $F_1=RM_T$ and $F_3=RQ_T$ are quasi-coherent Zariski modules, with canonical isomorphisms $LF_1\simeq M_T$ and $LF_3\simeq Q_T$. Put $E=RN_T$, an ordinary Zariski module, without assuming it quasi-coherent. The adjunction $L\dashv R$ of [lem-trf-etale-extension-free-presentations-hom] supplies the canonical counit $c:LE\to N_T$. On an etale $v:V\to T$, its local formula sends a scalar times a pulled-back section $a\otimes e$ to $a\,e|_V$. Naturality makes it compatible with both maps of the restricted short exact sequence.

source.place: Tag 06VE, lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-limits, proof of (10), restriction to the Zariski site and the comparison diagram.

proof.text: Let $W\subseteq T$ be any affine open. By Step 2, $M_T\simeq LF_1$, the associated sheaf of $F_1$ [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. Applying the etale restriction identification $(L_TF_1)|_{W_{\mathrm{et}}}\simeq L_W(F_1|_W)$ of [lem-trf-etale-extension-free-presentations-hom] to the open immersion $W\hookrightarrow T$, $M_T|_{W_{\mathrm{et}}}$ is the associated etale sheaf of $F_1|_W$. Thus [lem-sc-etale-affine-qcoherent], with $q=1$, gives $H^1(W_{\mathrm{et}},M_T|_{W_{\mathrm{et}}})=0$ for its underlying abelian sheaf. Forgetting module structures preserves the short exact sequence by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. Apply [lem-sc-lift-sections-h1-vanishing] to that sequence on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ and the object $W\hookrightarrow T$. It gives surjectivity $N_T(W)\to Q_T(W)$. The affine hypothesis is used only for this vanishing; the scheme $T$ itself need not be affine or quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 06VE, lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-limits, proof of (10), affine H^1 vanishing and exactness on the right.

proof.text: The sequence $0\to F_1\to E\to F_3\to0$ is short exact on the Zariski site. Indeed kernels are sectionwise by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], so restriction preserves the left part of the exact sequence. For any section of $F_3$ on any open, its restrictions to an affine open cover lift by Step 3; this is precisely local surjectivity, hence the right-hand map is an epimorphism of Zariski sheaves. Apply [lem-pc-quasi-coherent-extension] on the scheme $T$ to conclude that $E$ is quasi-coherent.

source.place: Tag 06VE, lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-limits, proof of (10), the restricted extension is quasi-coherent; schemes.tex Tag 01IE, lemma-extension-quasi-coherent.

proof.text: Now all three Zariski terms are quasi-coherent. By [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison], their associated sequence $0\to LF_1\to LE\to LF_3\to0$ is short exact in all small-etale module sheaves. The counits form a morphism from this sequence to $0\to M_T\to N_T\to Q_T\to0$. The end counits are isomorphisms by [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]; the middle counit is the $c$ of Step 2. The assertion of exactness used here is only for the small etale site, exactly the assertion of the cited node.

source.place: Tag 06VE, lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-limits, part (5) and proof of (10), comparison of the two exact rows.

proof.text: Here is the elementary chase in the diagram of Step 5. A local section of $LE$ killed by $c$ has zero image in $LF_3$, hence comes locally from $LF_1$; the left end isomorphism and injectivity of $M_T\to N_T$ force it to be zero. Conversely a section of $N_T$ has image in $Q_T$ which, through the right end isomorphism, lifts locally to $LE$; subtracting its image under $c$ leaves a section locally from $M_T$, which lifts through $LF_1\simeq M_T$. Thus $c$ is injective and locally surjective, hence an isomorphism. Since $E$ is quasi-coherent, so is $LE$, and therefore $N_T$, by [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence].

source.place: Tag 06VE, lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-limits, proof of (10), conclusion from the comparison diagram.

proof.text: Finally, the argument holds for every object $T\to X$. By [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], quasi-coherence of $N_T$ gives a covering of its final object $T$ on which $N_T$ has free presentations. In $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ these are the same coverings of $T$, the same restricted rings and the same presentations of $N$. This supplies the defining local presentations for every object of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, proving $N$ quasi-coherent. The argument also covers an empty chart (the empty covering is allowed) and imposes no global finiteness or separation condition on $X$.

source.place: Tag 03M1, lemma-properties-quasi-coherent, proof of (4); Tag 03M0, lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent, local-presentation conclusion.

proof_origin.place: Tag 03M1, lemma-properties-quasi-coherent, proof of (4), expanded using descent.tex Tag 0GNB (4) and Tag 06VE (5),(10), restricted throughout to the small etale site.
